question:
Which of the following metals was first used by man?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
Gold

Magnesium

Silver

Copper
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Copper

Explanation:
The first metal used by humans was Copper, dating back to around 9000 BCE. Copper was found in its pure form in nature and could be easily melted and shaped into tools. It was used during the prehistoric period to make weapons, ornaments, and utensils. After copper, humans began using Bronze (Copper + Tin), marking the beginning of the Bronze Age.

Extra Facts:
Copper's significance is evident in ancient civilizations like Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Indus Valley. The Indus Valley Civilization (2600-1900 BCE) had copper tools, statues, and jewelry. Additionally, evidence of ancient copper mines has been found in Khetri, Rajasthan.

☛ Silver - Used after copper and gold, mainly for decoration and coins
☛ Bronze Age - Alloy of copper and tin (3300-1200 BCE)
☛ Iron Age - Followed the Bronze Age (after 1500 BCE)
☛ Magnesium - A modern metal, unknown in ancient times
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किस धातु का सर्वप्रथम प्रयोग मनुष्य ने किया था?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi:
सोना

मैग्नीशियम

चांदी

तांबा
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है तांबा

Explanation:
मनुष्य द्वारा सर्वप्रथम प्रयोग की गई धातु तांबा (Copper) थी। यह लगभग 9000 ईसा पूर्व से प्रयोग में लाई जाने लगी। तांबा प्राकृतिक रूप से शुद्ध अवस्था में पाया जाता था और इसे आसानी से पिघलाकर औजार बनाया जा सकता था। इसका उपयोग प्रागैतिहासिक काल में हथियार, आभूषण और उपकरण बनाने के लिए किया गया। तांबे के बाद मनुष्य ने कांस्य (तांबा + टिन) का प्रयोग शुरू किया, जिससे कांस्य युग की शुरुआत हुई।

Extra Facts:
तांबे का महत्व प्राचीन सभ्यताओं जैसे मेसोपोटामिया, मिस्र और सिंधु घाटी में भी देखा जा सकता है। सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता (2600-1900 ईसा पूर्व) में तांबे के औजार, मूर्तियाँ और आभूषण पाए गए हैं। इसके अलावा, राजस्थान के खेतड़ी क्षेत्र में तांबे के प्राचीन खानों के साक्ष्य मिले हैं।

question:
Which of the following is a heritage site of Madhya Pradesh?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: Bhimbetka
Sasaram
Hampi
Lepakshi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhimbetka

Explanation:
Bhimbetka is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh. It is famous for its prehistoric rock paintings and caves, dating back approximately 30,000 years. The paintings depict human activities, animals, and daily life from the Stone Age. This site is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and provides significant research material for archaeologists.

Extra Facts:
The name Bhimbetka is associated with Bhima, a character from the Mahabharata. There are over 700 caves here, some containing paintings from the Mesolithic period to the historical era. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003.

☛ Sanchi Stupa - Buddhist site in MP, built by Ashoka.
question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन मध्य प्रदेश का एक विरासत स्थल है?

[SSC CGL 2019]
options_hi: भीमबेटका
सासाराम
हम्पी
लेपाक्षी
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है भीमबेटका

Explanation:
भीमबेटका मध्य प्रदेश के रायसेन जिले में स्थित एक यूनेस्को विश्व धरोहर स्थल है। यह प्रागैतिहासिक काल के शैल चित्रों और गुफाओं के लिए प्रसिद्ध है, जो लगभग 30,000 साल पुराने हैं। यहां पाए गए चित्र पाषाण युग की मानव गतिविधियों, जानवरों और दैनिक जीवन को दर्शाते हैं। यह स्थल भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण (ASI) द्वारा संरक्षित है और यहां की गुफाएं पुरातत्वविदों के लिए महत्वपूर्ण शोध सामग्री प्रदान करती हैं।

Extra Facts:
भीमबेटका का नाम महाभारत के चरित्र भीम से जुड़ा हुआ है। यहां लगभग 700 से अधिक गुफाएं हैं, जिनमें से कुछ में मध्य पाषाण युग से लेकर ऐतिहासिक काल तक के चित्र मिलते हैं। यह स्थल 2003 में यूनेस्को की विश्व धरोहर सूची में शामिल किया गया था।

question:
The Megalithic site __________ is a site on the river Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Hire benakal
Inamgaon
Hallur
Pottru
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Inamgaon

Explanation:
Inamgaon is a significant Megalithic archaeological site located on the banks of the Ghod River, a tributary of the Bhima. Situated in Pune district, Maharashtra, this site reveals evidence of an agrarian-based community. Excavations have uncovered pottery, tools, and human skeletons, providing insights into the socio-economic life of that era. Often referred to as the 'Mohenjo-Daro of Deccan,' Inamgaon offers crucial information about prehistoric cultures.

Extra Facts:
Inamgaon was excavated in 1968 by H.D. Sankalia. Findings suggest that its inhabitants cultivated wheat, barley, and pulses. The geometric designs on pottery reflect the artistic advancements of that period.

question_hi:
महापाषाण स्थल (Megalithic site) __________ घोड़ नदी, जो भीमा (Bhima) नदी की एक सहायक नदी है, पर स्थित एक स्थल है।

[SSC MTS 2024]
options_hi: हिरे बेनकाल (Hire benakal)
इनामगाँव (Inamgaon)
हल्लूर (Hallur)
पोट्रु (Pottru)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है इनामगाँव (Inamgaon)

Explanation:
इनामगाँव (Inamgaon) महापाषाण काल (Megalithic period) का एक प्रमुख पुरातात्विक स्थल है, जो घोड़ नदी (Ghod River) के किनारे स्थित है। यह स्थल महाराष्ट्र के पुणे जिले में स्थित है और यहाँ से प्राप्त अवशेषों से पता चलता है कि यह एक कृषि-आधारित समुदाय का केंद्र था। यहाँ मिट्टी के बर्तन, औजार, और मानव कंकाल मिले हैं, जो इस काल के सामाजिक-आर्थिक जीवन को समझने में मदद करते हैं। इनामगाँव को 'दक्कन का मोहनजोदड़ो' भी कहा जाता है क्योंकि यहाँ की खुदाई से प्रागैतिहासिक काल की महत्वपूर्ण जानकारी मिली है।

Extra Facts:
इनामगाँव की खुदाई 1968 में एच.डी. संकालिया (H.D. Sankalia) द्वारा की गई थी। यहाँ से मिले अवशेषों से पता चलता है कि यहाँ के लोग गेहूँ, जौ, और दालों की खेती करते थे। इसके अलावा, यहाँ से मिले मिट्टी के बर्तनों पर ज्यामितीय डिजाइन पाए गए हैं, जो इस काल के कलात्मक विकास को दर्शाते हैं।

question:
In which of the following places in Orissa will you find the cave architecture of the pre- historic times?

[CONSTABLE EXECUTIVE ]
options: Barbil
Baripada
Sisupalgarh
Jatni
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sisupalgarh

Explanation:
Sisupalgarh is an ancient historical site in Odisha where evidence of prehistoric cave architecture has been found. Located near Bhubaneswar, archaeological excavations here have revealed remnants from prehistoric times, including caves, rock paintings, and traces of human settlements. Sisupalgarh is considered an important center of the 'Kalinga' empire, and its caves indicate the early stages of human civilization.

Extra Facts:
Odisha has several prehistoric sites, with Sisupalgarh, Udayagiri, and Khandagiri being prominent. The caves of Sisupalgarh are not only architectural marvels but also symbols of ancient art and culture. The remnants found here suggest that this region was a hub of a developed civilization in ancient times.

उड़ीसा में प्रागैतिहासिक काल के कई स्थल हैं, जिनमें शिशुपालगढ़, उदयगिरि और खंडगिरि प्रमुख हैं। शिशुपालगढ़ की गुफाएँ न केवल वास्तुकला बल्कि प्राचीन कला और संस्कृति के भी प्रतीक हैं। यहाँ मिले अवशेषों से पता चलता है कि यह क्षेत्र प्राचीन काल में एक विकसित सभ्यता का केंद्र था।

question:
A celt is ______ from the Neolithic period.

[SSC CGL 2021]
options: a tomb
a house
a tool
an urn
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a tool

Explanation:
A celt is a tool from the Neolithic period, made of stone and used for cutting, digging, shaping wood, and other daily activities. The Neolithic Age (approx. 10,000-4,500 BCE) is also called the 'New Stone Age' because humans began crafting more refined stone tools during this era. The celt represents this technological advancement and played a crucial role in the development of agriculture and settlements.

Extra Facts:
The Neolithic Age marked the beginning of permanent human settlements and agriculture. Domestication of animals and weaving also emerged during this period. In India, key Neolithic sites include Burzahom (Kashmir), Mehrgarh (Balochistan), and Chirand (Bihar).

question_hi:
एक सेल्ट नवपाषाण काल से ______ है।

[SSC CGL 2021]
options_hi: एक मकबरा
एक घर
एक उपकरण
एक कलश
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है एक उपकरण

Explanation:
सेल्ट नवपाषाण काल (Neolithic Period) में प्रयुक्त होने वाला एक महत्वपूर्ण उपकरण था। यह पत्थर से बना होता था और इसका उपयोग काटने, खोदने, लकड़ी को आकार देने तथा अन्य दैनिक कार्यों के लिए किया जाता था। नवपाषाण काल (लगभग 10,000-4,500 ईसा पूर्व) को 'नए पत्थर का युग' कहा जाता है, क्योंकि इस दौरान मानव ने पत्थर के उपकरणों को अधिक परिष्कृत तरीके से बनाना शुरू किया। सेल्ट इसी तकनीकी विकास का एक उदाहरण है। यह कृषि और बस्तियों के विकास में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता था।

Extra Facts:
नवपाषाण काल में मानव ने स्थायी निवास बनाना शुरू किया और कृषि का विकास हुआ। इस युग में पहली बार पशुपालन और बुनाई जैसी गतिविधियाँ भी शुरू हुईं। भारत में बुर्जहोम (कश्मीर), मेहरगढ़ (बलूचिस्तान) और चिरांद (बिहार) जैसी साइट्स नवपाषाण संस्कृति के प्रमुख केंद्र थे।

question:
Bhimbetka, a noted site of the Palaeolithic period, is located in which state of India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options:
Bihar

Uttar Pradesh

Rajasthan

Madhya Pradesh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madhya Pradesh

Explanation:
Bhimbetka is a significant archaeological site from the Palaeolithic period, located in Madhya Pradesh, India. It is situated in the Raisen district, on the southern edge of the Vindhya Range. Recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003, Bhimbetka is renowned for its rock paintings, which date back approximately 30,000 years. These paintings depict animals, dances, hunting scenes, and religious rituals, offering insights into early human civilization.

Extra Facts:
The name Bhimbetka is associated with Bhima, a character from the Mahabharata. Local legends suggest that Bhima rested here. The site contains around 750 rock shelters, with paintings found in over 400 of them, spanning from the Stone Age to the Medieval period.

question:
Pottery was first traceable to which period of ancient Indian history?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Chalcolithic
Palaeolithic
Neolithic
Mesolithic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Neolithic

Explanation:
Pottery was first traceable to the Neolithic Age in ancient Indian history. This period is estimated to be around 7000 BCE to 1000 BCE. During this era, humans learned agriculture and started settling in permanent dwellings. The invention of pottery marked a significant advancement, as it was used for cooking and storing food. Sites like Burzahom (Kashmir) and Chirand (Bihar) have yielded Neolithic pottery.

Extra Facts:
The Neolithic Age is also called the 'Agricultural Revolution' period because humans began farming for the first time. People used polished stone tools, which were more refined than earlier periods. Mehrgarh (Pakistan) contains some of the earliest Neolithic evidence in South Asia.

Explanation:
The Mesolithic Period in Indian history is roughly dated from 12,000 years ago to 10,000 years ago. This era marks the transition between the Paleolithic and Neolithic ages. Key developments during this period include the use of smaller and more refined stone tools (microliths), the beginning of animal domestication, and the emergence of early art forms (e.g., Bhimbetka rock paintings). It also signifies the shift of humans toward a semi-sedentary lifestyle.

Extra Facts:
The Mesolithic era is also called the Microlithic Age due to the prevalence of microliths (tiny stone tools). People relied on hunting and gathering but gradually moved toward agriculture. Major Indian Mesolithic sites include Bagor (Rajasthan), Langhnaj (Gujarat), and Sarai Nahar Rai (Uttar Pradesh).

[SSC MTS 2022]

solution:

Explanation:
The prehistoric period in the early development of human beings is commonly known as the Old Stone Age (Paleolithic Age). This era is estimated to have lasted from 2.6 million years ago to around 10,000 BCE. During this period, humans used primitive stone tools such as scrapers, hammerstones, and hand axes. The lifestyle was based on hunting and gathering, and humans lived in caves. Key archaeological sites from this age include Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) and Hunsgi (Karnataka). This was the longest and earliest phase of human civilization.

Extra Facts:
The Paleolithic Age is divided into three phases - Lower, Middle, and Upper Paleolithic. Humans learned to use fire during this period, which revolutionized their survival. Species like Homo erectus and Homo sapiens evolved in this era. It laid the foundation for human cultural and technological progress.

The Palaeolithic period extends from 2 million years ago to about 12,000 years ago. This long stretch of time is divided into the Lower, Middle and Upper Palaeolithic. This long span of time covers________percent of human history.

solution:

Explanation:
The Palaeolithic period is the longest phase of human history, spanning from 2 million years ago to around 12,000 years ago. This era marks the early stages of human evolution, where humans learned to make stone tools and relied on hunting and gathering. It covers approximately 99% of human history because subsequent periods like the Neolithic and the rise of civilizations occurred in a relatively much shorter time frame.

Extra Facts:
The Palaeolithic period is divided into three phases - Lower, Middle, and Upper Palaeolithic. Humans during this time were nomadic and lived in caves. In India, evidence of this era has been found at sites like Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) and Adamgarh (Madhya Pradesh).

question:
Which of the following periods succeeds the Palaeolithic period?

[RPF SI 2024]
options: Neolithic
Mesolithic
Iron Age
Chalcolithic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mesolithic

Explanation:
The Palaeolithic Age (Old Stone Age) was the earliest period of human history, spanning from around 2.6 million years ago to 10,000 BCE. It was followed by the Mesolithic Age (Middle Stone Age), which lasted from approximately 10,000 BCE to 6,000 BCE. This period marked a transitional phase in the Stone Age, characterized by the use of smaller and more refined stone tools. Humans during this era relied on hunting and gathering but also began experimenting with early forms of agriculture. The Neolithic Age (New Stone Age) succeeded the Mesolithic period, witnessing the full development of agriculture and animal domestication.

Extra Facts:
The Mesolithic Age is also called the 'Microlithic Age' due to the widespread use of small, sharp stone tools (microliths). During this period, humans domesticated the dog for the first time. In India, significant Mesolithic sites include Bagor (Rajasthan) and Adamgarh (Madhya Pradesh). This era was closely linked to climatic changes and the end of the Ice Age.

question:
Into how many ages is the prehistoric times in terms of technology divided ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: Five
Six
Three
Four
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Three

Explanation:
The prehistoric period is divided into three ages based on technology - Stone Age, Bronze Age, and Iron Age. This classification is based on the primary materials used for tools and weapons. The Stone Age saw the use of stone tools, while the Bronze Age marked the advent of metal (bronze) tools. The Iron Age introduced iron tools, revolutionizing agriculture and warfare. This division is crucial for understanding the evolution of human civilization.

Extra Facts:
The Stone Age is further subdivided into three phases - Paleolithic, Mesolithic, and Neolithic. The Bronze Age witnessed the rise of the Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan Civilization), known for its bronze tools and weapons. The Iron Age saw the emergence of powerful empires like the Mauryan Empire, marking a new era in Indian history.

question:
In which type of Megalith (grave/memorial) were the stone pieces set in a circular shape around the grave?

[SSC MTS ]
options: Cairn circle
Dolmen
Rock cut cave
Menhir
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cairn circle

Explanation:
A Cairn circle is a type of megalithic structure where stone pieces are arranged in a circular pattern around a grave. This practice was prevalent during the Iron Age in ancient India, particularly in South India. These structures were used as burial sites and often contained human remains, pottery, and other grave goods. Their construction reflects the social and religious significance of death rituals during that period.

Extra Facts:
The Megalithic Culture flourished roughly between 1200 BCE and 300 CE, prominently in Deccan, South India, and Northeast India. A Dolmen is another megalithic structure where large stones are arranged in a table-like formation. Menhirs are single standing stones, often serving as memorials or religious symbols.

संगोरा वृत्त (Cairn Circle) एक प्रकार की महापाषाण संरचना है जिसमें कब्र के चारों ओर पत्थर के टुकड़ों को गोलाकार आकृति में व्यवस्थित किया जाता था। यह प्रथा प्राचीन भारत में लौह युग (Iron Age) के दौरान प्रचलित थी, विशेषकर दक्षिण भारत में। ये संरचनाएँ मृतकों के दफन स्थल के रूप में उपयोग की जाती थीं और इनमें अक्सर मानव अस्थियाँ, मिट्टी के बर्तन और अन्य कब्र सामग्री पाई जाती थीं। इनका निर्माण सामाजिक और धार्मिक महत्व को दर्शाता है, जो उस समय की मृत्यु संबंधी मान्यताओं को प्रतिबिंबित करता है।

Extra Facts:
महापाषाण संस्कृति (Megalithic Culture) मुख्यतः 1200 ईसा पूर्व से 300 ईस्वी तक फैली हुई थी। यह संस्कृति विशेष रूप से दक्कन, दक्षिण भारत और पूर्वोत्तर भारत में प्रमुख थी। डोलमेन (Dolmen) एक अन्य प्रकार की महापाषाण संरचना है, जिसमें बड़े पत्थरों को एक टेबल जैसी आकृति में रखा जाता था। मेनहिर (Menhir) एकल खड़े पत्थरों से बनी स्मारक संरचनाएँ थीं, जो अक्सर स्मृति चिह्न के रूप में काम करती थीं।

question:
Which of the following sites is better known as a Chalcolithic Site ?

[RPF SI 2024]
options: Utnur
Kayatha
Burzahom
Mehrgarh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Kayatha

Explanation:
Kayatha is a prominent Chalcolithic site located in the Ujjain district of Madhya Pradesh. Dating back to 2000-1800 BCE, this site has yielded copper tools, pottery, and other archaeological remains. The Kayatha culture is considered an important Chalcolithic culture, predating the Malwa culture. The inhabitants practiced agriculture and animal husbandry, and their pottery featured distinctive red and black paintings.

Extra Facts:
The Chalcolithic Age marked the transition from the Neolithic to the Bronze Age, with humans beginning to use copper alongside stone tools. This era saw the development of agriculture, domestication of animals, and settled village life. In India, other significant Chalcolithic cultures include Ahar-Banas, Jorwe, and Malwa. Besides Kayatha, sites like Navdatoli and Eran are also notable Chalcolithic settlements.

question:
In which among the following period Catal Huyuk was one of the most famous sites?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Neolithic
Mesolithic
Palaeolithic
Chalcolithic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Neolithic

Explanation:
Catal Huyuk is a major archaeological site belonging to the Neolithic Age (around 7500-5700 BCE). Located in Anatolia, Turkey, it is considered one of the world's oldest and best-preserved Neolithic settlements. Evidence of agriculture, animal domestication, and permanent housing—hallmarks of the Neolithic period—has been found here. The site's wall paintings, sculptures, and multi-story houses reflect the advanced civilization of this era.

Extra Facts:
Catal Huyuk was discovered in 1958 by James Mellaart. Its inhabitants cultivated wheat, barley, and peas and domesticated sheep, goats, and cattle. A unique feature of this site is that houses had no doors; entry was through roofs. It is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

question:
During which of the following period Ostriches were found in India?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Mesolithic
Chalcolithic
Neolithic
Palaeolithic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Palaeolithic

Explanation:
Ostrich eggs and bones have been discovered at archaeological sites belonging to the Palaeolithic Age in India. This period is estimated to have lasted from around 2.6 million years ago to 10,000 BCE. During this era, humans were hunter-gatherers and relied on wild animals for survival. Sites like Bhimbetka (Madhya Pradesh) and Adamgarh have yielded ostrich remains, proving the existence of this large bird in ancient India.

Extra Facts:
The Palaeolithic Age is divided into three phases - Lower, Middle, and Upper Palaeolithic. Early humans developed stone tool-making techniques during this time. Species like Homo erectus and later Homo sapiens emerged in this period. Large birds like ostriches thrived in the then-environment but became extinct due to climatic changes.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से किस युग के दौरान भारत में शुतुरमुर्ग पाए गए थे?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options_hi: मध्यपाषाण काल
ताम्रपाषाण युग
नवपाषाण युग
पुरापाषाण युग
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है पुरापाषाण युग

Explanation:
भारत में शुतुरमुर्ग के अंडे और हड्डियाँ पुरापाषाण युग (Palaeolithic Age) के पुरातात्विक स्थलों से प्राप्त हुई हैं। यह युग लगभग 2.6 मिलियन वर्ष पूर्व से 10,000 ईसा पूर्व तक माना जाता है। इस काल में मानव शिकारी-संग्रहकर्ता था और जंगली जानवरों पर निर्भर रहता था। भीमबेटका (मध्य प्रदेश) और आदमगढ़ जैसे स्थलों से शुतुरमुर्ग के अवशेष मिले हैं, जो इस बात का प्रमाण देते हैं कि भारत में इस विशाल पक्षी का अस्तित्व था।

Extra Facts:
पुरापाषाण युग को तीन चरणों में बाँटा जाता है - निम्न, मध्य और उच्च पुरापाषाण काल। इस दौरान मानव ने पत्थर के औजार बनाने की कला विकसित की। होमो इरेक्टस और बाद में होमो सेपियन्स जैसी मानव प्रजातियाँ इसी युग में उभरीं। शुतुरमुर्ग जैसे बड़े पक्षी उस समय के वातावरण के अनुकूल थे, जो बाद में जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण विलुप्त हो गए।
